plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of slender silver-green stems topped with dense spikes of violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and release a sweet, herbal perfume across the fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, with peak bloom in early to mid July
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Tilia cordata
plants.description: A stately shade tree that, in early summer, hangs clusters of small, creamy-yellow flowers beneath pale bracts. Their honeyed fragrance drifts down city streets and woodland edges.
plants.location: Temperate Europe, including Germany, Poland and the UK
plants.funFact: Linden flowers are one of the most prized nectar sources for bees, and they are also dried for a soothing herbal tea.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged coastal tree whose chunky, candle-like flower spikes glow in greenish-gold and silver. Honeyeaters and native bees crowd around the blooms through the Southern Hemisphere winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to winter, in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly February to July)
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are woody and often open fully only after bushfire, which releases the seeds onto freshly cleared, nutrient-rich ground.
